sections.title: Build Overview
paragraphs: The advertised “zero-button” label describes the finished map loop, not character setup. You still maintain two buffs, build Glory, arrange the Rage and Endurance recovery loop, and create Molten Crash fissures. In 0.5, Ancestral Cry steps and Walking Calamity no longer trigger Fire Spell on Hit or Cast on Elemental Ailment directly; walking over Molten Crash fissures is the current trigger path described by the maintained guide.

That change matters because an old video can look visually identical while using a dead trigger source. The safe baseline is to confirm fissure creation, walk-over detonation, Living Bomb and the fire-infused Comet chain one step at a time before adding the expensive low-input automation.

sections.title: Mapping
paragraphs: Maintain the required buffs, create fissures with Molten Crash, then move through them with Ancestral Cry active so the remaining trigger chain can occur. If the screen is quiet, inspect fissures first; walking without a fissure is no longer sufficient.

sections.title: Bossing
paragraphs: Pre-create fissures with Molten Crash and, where used, Forge Hammer on the second weapon set. Add the armour-break or damage-buff layer only after the trigger chain is visible. A boss attempt is a poor place to discover that the character is merely walking over empty ground.
Track Rage, Glory and Endurance Charges before claiming a permanent loop.

items.question: Why do I walk through enemies without triggering the fire package?
answer: In 0.5, walking or Ancestral Cry steps alone are not the trigger. Confirm that Molten Crash created fissures and that you are walking over those fissures with the correct skills socketed.
bullets: Test on one stationary rare.

items.question: Is this truly zero-button?
answer: Only after setup, buff maintenance and charge recovery work. Calling the leveling build zero-button hides the preparation and leads to expensive purchases before the loop exists.

items.question: What if I want a simpler Bear route?
answer: Rampage Shaman has active Rage and animation management but a more direct attack loop without the same fire-trigger dependency.
